## 🎯 Objectives

By the end of this tutorial, you will be able to:

* connect a Shiny input to an output;
* simulate repeated coin flips; and
* use one reactive expression in more than one output.

::: {.callout-important}
## What you will build

You will build **one small app**, one piece at a time. Each time the user presses a button, the app will flip a biased coin 100 times, show the outcomes and calculate the proportion of heads.

Do not try to write the complete app at once. Run the app after every small change.
:::

## Preparation

You need the `shiny` and `bslib` packages. Install them in the Console if you do not already have them:

```r
install.packages(c("shiny", "bslib"))
```

Create a new folder called `coin-app`. Inside that folder, create a blank file called `app.R`.

## The question behind the app

Imagine a coin for which the probability of heads is 0.8. We flip it 100 times and estimate the probability of heads as:

> number of heads ÷ 100

Even though the true probability stays at 0.8, the estimate will not be exactly 0.8 every time. Our app will let a user repeat the experiment and see this variation.

## 1. Start with the app skeleton

Copy the following code into `app.R`.

```r
library(shiny)
library(bslib)

ui <- page_sidebar(
  title = "How much does an estimate change?",
  sidebar = sidebar(
    # We will put an input here.
  ),
  card(
    card_header("Flip a biased coin 100 times"),
    p("The probability of heads is 0.8."),
    # We will put outputs here.
  )
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  # We will add the app's instructions here.
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```

Run the app. You should see a title, an empty sidebar and a card containing some text.

The packages come first, `ui` describes the page, `server` describes what happens, and `shinyApp(ui, server)` assembles the app.

## 2. Practise flipping the coin in R

Before using Shiny, complete this ordinary R code. Replace the blanks so it makes 100 flips, samples with replacement, and gives heads probability 0.8 and tails probability 0.2.

```r
flips <- sample(
  c("H", "T"),
  size = _____,
  replace = _____,
  prob = c(_____, _____)
)
```

::: {.unilur-solution}
## Simulate 100 flips

```r
flips <- sample(
  c("H", "T"),
  size = 100,
  replace = TRUE,
  prob = c(0.8, 0.2)
)
```

The values in `prob` match the order of the outcomes: 0.8 belongs to `"H"` and 0.2 belongs to `"T"`.
:::

Run `flips`, then use this comparison to check which results are heads:

```r
flips == "H"
```

R treats `TRUE` as 1 and `FALSE` as 0 when calculating a mean. Calculate the proportion of heads.

::: {.unilur-solution}
## Calculate the estimate

```r
mean(flips == "H")
```

For example, if 79 of the 100 results are heads, the mean of the 79 `TRUE` values and 21 `FALSE` values is 0.79.
:::

## 3. Give the user a button

Return to `app.R`. Replace the comment inside `sidebar()` with an action button.

::: {.callout-tip}
The pattern for a button is:

```r
actionButton("input_id", "Label shown to the user")
```

The first string is the ID used by the server. The second string is the text displayed on the button.
:::

Your button should:

* have the input ID `"flip"`; and
* display the label **Flip coin 100 times**.

::: {.unilur-solution}
## Add the input

```r
sidebar = sidebar(
  actionButton("flip", "Flip coin 100 times")
)
```
:::

Run the app and press the button. Nothing else changes yet because the server has no instructions for it.

::: {.callout-note}
The string `"flip"` is the **input ID**. Inside the server, its value is available as `input$flip`.

An action button starts at 0. Each press increases its value by 1.
:::

## 4. Reserve places for the results

Replace the output comment inside `card()` with the following headings:

```r
h4("Estimate"),
# Put the estimate output here.
h4("The 100 outcomes"),
# Put the outcomes output here.
```

Under the first heading, add `textOutput()` with the output ID `"estimate"`. Under the second heading, add another `textOutput()` with the ID `"flips"`.

::: {.unilur-solution}
## Add the output places

```r
card(
  card_header("Flip a biased coin 100 times"),
  p("The probability of heads is 0.8."),
  h4("Estimate"),
  textOutput("estimate"),
  h4("The 100 outcomes"),
  textOutput("flips")
)
```
:::

Run the app again. `textOutput()` reserves a place on the page; it does not create the text.

## 5. Make the first connection

We will first use the estimate output to check that the button and server are connected.

Inside `server()`, add:

```r
output$estimate <- renderText({
  paste("The button has been pressed", input$flip, "times.")
})
```

Run the app and press the button twice. Trace the path:

`actionButton("flip", ...)` → `input$flip` → `renderText()` → `output$estimate` → `textOutput("estimate")`

The input ID `"flip"` becomes `input$flip`. The output ID `"estimate"` becomes `output$estimate`. These names must match exactly.

## 6. Generate a new batch after each press

The app needs one batch of 100 flips that can be used by both outputs. Replace the contents of `server()` with this skeleton:

```r
server <- function(input, output, session) {
  flips <- reactive({
    if (input$flip == 0) {
      return(character(0))
    }

    # Simulate and return 100 flips here.
  })
}
```

Copy your `sample()` code from Step 2 into the marked position. Do not assign it to another object: the last expression in the reactive block is the value it returns.

::: {.unilur-solution}
## Create the reactive flips

```r
server <- function(input, output, session) {
  flips <- reactive({
    if (input$flip == 0) {
      return(character(0))
    }

    sample(
      c("H", "T"),
      size = 100,
      replace = TRUE,
      prob = c(0.8, 0.2)
    )
  })
}
```
:::

Before the first press, `input$flip` is 0 and the reactive expression returns an empty character vector. After a press, `input$flip` changes and the code runs again.

::: {.callout-warning}
`flips` is a reactive expression, not an ordinary vector. Inside the server, get its current value by writing `flips()` with parentheses.
:::

## 7. Calculate and display the estimate

After the closing `})` of the reactive expression, but still inside `server()`, recreate `output$estimate`.

Complete the three blanks in this skeleton:

```r
output$estimate <- renderText({
  if (input$flip == 0) {
    return("Press the button to run the experiment.")
  }

  # Replace each blank with the required R code.
  results <- _____
  estimate <- _____

  paste("Estimated probability of heads:", _____)
})
```

::: {.unilur-solution}
## Render the estimate

```r
output$estimate <- renderText({
  if (input$flip == 0) {
    return("Press the button to run the experiment.")
  }

  results <- flips()
  estimate <- mean(results == "H")

  paste("Estimated probability of heads:", round(estimate, 2))
})
```
:::

Run the app. It should display an instruction at first and a new estimate after every press.

## 8. Display the individual outcomes

We also reserved `textOutput("flips")` in the UI. Create its matching server output with `renderText()`.

Use:

```r
paste(flips(), collapse = " ")
```

to turn the vector of outcomes into one piece of text with spaces between the values. As with the estimate, show an instruction before the first press.

::: {.unilur-solution}
## Render the outcomes

```r
output$flips <- renderText({
  if (input$flip == 0) {
    return("The outcomes will appear here.")
  }

  paste(flips(), collapse = " ")
})
```
:::

Run the app and press the button. Do the displayed outcomes and estimate come from the same experiment?

::: {.callout-note}
Both outputs call `flips()`. Shiny therefore generates one batch for each press and lets both outputs use it. Separate calls to `sample()` in the two outputs could produce results that do not agree.
:::

::: {.unilur-solution}
## 9. Check the complete app

Compare your `app.R` with the complete version below. Before replacing anything, locate the differences and decide whether they matter.

```r
library(shiny)
library(bslib)

ui <- page_sidebar(
  title = "How much does an estimate change?",
  sidebar = sidebar(
    actionButton("flip", "Flip coin 100 times")
  ),
  card(
    card_header("Flip a biased coin 100 times"),
    p("The probability of heads is 0.8."),
    h4("Estimate"),
    textOutput("estimate"),
    h4("The 100 outcomes"),
    textOutput("flips")
  )
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  flips <- reactive({
    if (input$flip == 0) {
      return(character(0))
    }

    sample(
      c("H", "T"),
      size = 100,
      replace = TRUE,
      prob = c(0.8, 0.2)
    )
  })

  output$estimate <- renderText({
    if (input$flip == 0) {
      return("Press the button to run the experiment.")
    }

    results <- flips()
    estimate <- mean(results == "H")

    paste("Estimated probability of heads:", round(estimate, 2))
  })

  output$flips <- renderText({
    if (input$flip == 0) {
      return("The outcomes will appear here.")
    }

    paste(flips(), collapse = " ")
  })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)
```
:::

Check that one press produces 100 outcomes, that the estimate agrees with them, and that another press replaces both results.

## Optional extension: count the heads (5 minutes)

Add one more output that reports the number of heads, for example:

> Number of heads: 83 out of 100

This output must use the existing `flips()` reactive expression. It should not call `sample()` again.

First, add a heading and output place inside `card()` in the UI:

```r
h4("Number of heads"),
textOutput("heads")
```

Then add the matching `output$heads` inside the server. These two expressions will help:

```r
sum(flips() == "H")
paste("Number of heads:", number_of_heads, "out of 100")
```

Remember to display an instruction rather than a count before the first button press.

::: {.unilur-solution}
## Count the heads

```r
output$heads <- renderText({
  if (input$flip == 0) {
    return("The count will appear here.")
  }

  number_of_heads <- sum(flips() == "H")
  paste("Number of heads:", number_of_heads, "out of 100")
})
```
:::

## If your app does not work

1. Read the **first error** in the R Console.
2. Check the most recent code you added, including commas and brackets.
3. Check that `"flip"`, `"estimate"` and `"flips"` match everywhere.
4. Check that you read the reactive value with parentheses: `flips()`.

::: {.callout-tip}
If the app opens but part of the page is blank, trace that output backwards:

`textOutput("estimate")` ← `output$estimate` ← `renderText()` ← the values used inside it.
:::

## Wrap-up

For the coin-flipping app:

* the **input** is the button press;
* the shared **reactive value** is the batch of 100 flips; and
* the **outputs** are two text views of that batch.

The important pattern is:

`UI input` → `server calculation` → `UI output`
